newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bull market climbs to feet, hits records.
newsitem.headline: Russian bull market climbs to feet, hits records.

text.p: Russian shares ended two months in the doldrums, breaking index and individual records on Monday, and share analysts said the market's retreat had ended.
Market bellwether national electric company UES jumped over 20 percent on the Russian Trading System (RTS) on the debut of global depositary receipts, share-look alikes which trade outside Russia.
UES RTS shares finished the day at $0.3140, off a daily high and record of over 34 cents and up from $0.2798 on Thursday, the last trading day in Russia. It was eight cents in early December.
The RTS 22-share index gained 6.9 percent to close at a record 360.72.
"The Dow is already up where it was pre-Fed Rate hike, so where is the risk?" said CentreInvest research chief James Fenkner. "The big question with Russia was uncertainty in the West."
The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates by 25 basis points on March 25, sending Western markets into decline and pulling investors' focus from Russia.

Fenkner predicted the RTS index would see 400 by next month, but said UES and the market would probably cool off for a couple of days. The market would move ahead but not see a repeat of the beginning-of-year surge, he said.
Leading investors were conducting massive value-hunts among companies outside the telecoms, utilities and oil sectors and those companies would see the sharpest gains, he said.
"The hunt has begun for large companies outside the three main sectors -- and it is a structural hunt now."
Another share analyst at a Western brokerage in Moscow confirmed Western fund buying, which pushed the index up about 75 percent in the first two months of the year, had resumed.
"It's all New York," the analyst said. "Russia is back in vogue, emerging market funds are increasing, and people are willing to pay higher multiples (for Russian shares)."
He said the market would gain about five percent by the end of the month, led by a dozen shares with high enough liquidity to absorb substantial new funds.

Analysts said a new wave of American and Global depositary receipts were promised for the year, but the Western brokerage analyst said top liquid shares, unlike UES, would not see sharp gains from the ADRs.
"The reason UES is doing well is not that it is illiquid but that people just want to have a hand on it."
Troika Dialog research director Gavin Rankin said power utilities, following UES's re-evaluation, were well positioned for the near term.
"Energos (power utilities) will follow UES because they are all interrelated," he said. "A lot of them are below their all- time highs -- there is still movement to come."
He pointed to leading liquid power companies, such as Moscow regional provider Mosenergo and Siberian provider Irkutskenergo.

But he said a new wave of investment had not yet poured down on Russia, which had seen volumes above $40 million, the average during the January-February boom, only rarely recently. Share turnover was $50 million on Monday.
"A one-off $40 million is not going to create an average of $40 million," Rankin said.
